# VTT Caption Generator

- Route: `/tools/generate-vtt-captions`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `generate-vtt-captions`

## Summary

Create a .vtt caption file for HTML5 video, YouTube or a player with AI transcription on our own GPU servers. (AI tools)

## Details

WebVTT is the caption format of the web: the HTML5 track element, YouTube, Vimeo, HLS and DASH players all read it. Media Manipulator generates timed VTT captions from any video or audio with a Whisper model on a GPU server we operate, so your media never goes to a third-party AI, and opens the result in a caption viewer where you can check the timing before downloading.
### What it does
- Transcribes speech and segments it into timed cues.
- Outputs a standards-compliant .vtt file.
- Detects the language automatically.
- Runs on our own GPU; no third-party AI provider.
### How to use it
1. Upload video or audio: Any common format.
2. Keep VTT selected: Or switch to SRT, text or JSON.
3. Transcribe: Whisper times each cue.
4. Download: Attach the .vtt to your player.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, m4v, flv, wmv, mp3, wav, m4a
- Output: vtt, srt, txt, json
- Each caption file counts as one AI job; failed jobs are not counted.
### Technical details
- Cues follow Whisper's segmentation, typically one sentence or clause per cue of 2 to 7 seconds.
- Translate the result into other languages with the Caption translator.
- For a burned-in caption track, use Darkroom's caption lane.
### Use cases
- HTML5 video: Attach the file with a track element.
- YouTube upload: Upload the .vtt as a caption track.
- Course video: Captions for an LMS player.
- Translate later: VTT in, translated VTT out.
### FAQ
Q: VTT or SRT?
A: VTT for web players and YouTube; SRT for video editors and some older platforms. Both are offered.
Q: Can I edit the captions?
A: Download the .vtt and edit it in any text editor; the format is plain text.
Q: Can I translate them?
A: Yes, with the Caption translator tool.
Q: Is my video sent to a third party?
A: No. Transcription runs on our own GPU server.
Q: Does this count against my allowance?
A: Each VTT file is one AI job, taken from the AI allowance and never from the everyday one. Failed jobs are not counted.
